convoLines.text: «Hei! Du... hva heter du?» "Water?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
On the way, Mia stops and actually teaches you something — how they read a slope for water, how their grandmother did it. (Knowledge, freely given. The Codex notes it.)
«Godt sagt. Helt riktig.» They nod back, a little quicker this time.
«Dette glemmer jeg deg aldri.» (you catch 'glemmer' — forget, 'aldri' — never) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Du er et godt menneske.» (you catch 'godt' — good) You point at yourself, then at them, then at the fire. Together. They get it.
You lean in, catching the rise and fall of it. «Hvor sover man her? Er det trygt?» (you catch 'trygt' — safe)
Mia lights up. "No, no — like this." They say it slowly, twice, watching your mouth shape it. "Akkurat sånn. Helt riktig." You try again. Closer. They grin like you just scored the winning point.
They take it in and give nothing back. Not yet.
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I asked Molly about the pantry run — Molly's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. I know the far treeline, past the rocks — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
Move next to your partner, on the same side of the Haven door.
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"I wasn't a rail conductor. I was an exterminator. The less of me is out there, the less can be used against me."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
They nod — and keep their distance, for now.
"No, yeah, of course. Forget I asked." They won't forget. They'll let it rest — for now.
"Still on that foraging help."
"That again?" Amanda sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
"Right. Go on, then."
"No — you're right, it's a lot. Forget it."
"See you around."
"Can I tell you something? At night I cry quietly so no one hears."
"Thank you for hearing it. I needed someone to know — and I needed it to stop with you. That is all."
"Me? Okay." "Listen. I need you to hear this before you go back out there."
"You've seen what's out there. I'm just saying — the treeline at dusk. Don't."
"Good. I mean it — watch yourself out there."
"I keep thinking about that Judge Hoot. It knows this ground now. Keep your eyes up past the treeline."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Molly always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"I clean up other people's messes quietly. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Still on what's been happening, as it were."
"Another time. The village needs me here."
"Rest when you can. We'll talk again soon."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
«Godt at du er her. Virkelig.» (you catch 'Godt' — good)

«Alt blir bra.» (Everything will be good. — you're fairly sure) You press a hand to your own chest, then point at them. Together — they get it.
You hold still and let the sounds settle. «Forstår du?» (Do you understand? — you're fairly sure)
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about that wound care — we got cut off, 4 days back."
"I can't reach this properly. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"Every day it's angrier. I need it cleaned before it turns — I can't work a wound like this. Wrap it tight when you're done."
Get to their side of the Haven door and stand next to them — then you can help.
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"Since Molly died... I keep expecting to see Molly at the fire. Stupid."
"Another time. The village needs me here."
You show them Spicebush — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I keep turning over the last thing Molly said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.

lines: d40: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Molly Banks is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d40: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d40: 🕯️ Molly is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d40: Stonebridge watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer. (Trust -8.
d40: 🕯️ Molly Banks is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d40: What Molly kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d40: "Molly's gone." Vikram looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Molly." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d40: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Finn blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d40: 📖 LEARNED: Generous Heart (Level 1). Donating gives 2x trust.
d40: 📖 LEARNED: Mediation (Level 1). Let each side talk without interruption. Repeat back what you heard. People de-escalate when heard.
d40: 📖 LEARNED: Soft Step (Level 1). Move through woods like weather. Less noise, fewer surprises.
d40: 📖 LEARNED: Animal Behavior (Level 1). Most animals flee. Give them an escape route and they take it. Cornered animals fight.
d40: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d40: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Molly Banks, 40 days. The mantle passes to Finn Bruno.
d40: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Finn Bruno, 63 — a Social worker. Their hands know different work now: Green Whisper, Scream Cheese.
d40: The village's quarrel was with Molly — and Molly is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d40: At the grave, Amanda, Vikram, Max and 7 more speak for Finn — "Molly trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d40: The fire knew Finn before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
